subject.title: Feature: Dynamic identity resolution for allowlists (dmPolicy: dynamic)

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared dynamic sender authorization seam for channel DM/group ingress, and should it be modeled as dynamic access-group membership rather than new dmPolicy/groupPolicy modes?
rationale: The need is valid, but the permanent API changes config, plugin SDK, channel authorization, and security failure semantics in ways automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Extend ingress access groups
options.body: Add a shared dynamic access-group resolver contract with explicit fail-closed semantics, then wire iMessage or plugin-owned resolvers through that seam.

options.title: Add dynamic policy modes
options.body: Add dmPolicy/groupPolicy dynamic plus resolver config directly, accepting a larger config surface and possible overlap with access groups.

options.title: Decline core resolver
options.body: Keep current static access groups and pairing behavior, and require external operators to sync allowFrom through existing config or plugin-specific tools.

recommendation.title: Extend ingress access groups
recommendation.body: Add a shared dynamic access-group resolver contract with explicit fail-closed semantics, then wire iMessage or plugin-owned resolvers through that seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points to shared channel ingress, access-groups, and iMessage authorization seams where this product/API choice would land.
